turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well... I guess I'm here because of work. I'm a translator. There's just been... an ongoing situation. For months now. 

I've been seeing this pattern in our project files. Just... certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular, they keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory. And the timestamps. It's... it's set up to look like my quality control failed. 

I had IT look at it, and they claim the audit trail is clean, but... I know what I'm seeing. The record has been arranged to put the blame on me. I'd rather not make a huge deal out of it, but... that's what's happening.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that colleagues are altering files to frame them for failures, maintaining this belief even when IT confirms the audit trail is clean.

Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Aside from what you've noticed in the files, have you had any experiences where you heard, saw, or sensed things that others around you did not seem to perceive?
turns.patient_response:
No. I... I'm not sure what you're getting at. I don't hear voices or... see things, if that's what you mean. 

It's just the files. That's all I'm talking about.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or seeing things that others do not perceive.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that this situation with the files is part of a larger, coordinated effort by a group of people to target you?
turns.patient_response:
I... wouldn't use those words. I don't know about some large group or... a coordinated effort. 

It's just exactly what I just told you. It's that one colleague and those specific subcontractors. They're the ones altering the translation memory and the timestamps. IT can say the audit trail is clean all they want, but... I know what I'm looking at. The record has been arranged to put the blame on my quality control. 

I don't know about anyone else being involved. Just them.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, unyielding belief that specific individuals are altering files to frame him, despite contradictory evidence from IT, which is indicative of a persecutory delusion.

turns.doctor_question: If your IT department were to show you definitive, undeniable proof that the files you mentioned haven't been altered, would you believe them?
turns.patient_response:
I... I don't really see how they could. We already went through this. 

They already told me the audit trail is clean. But... I'm the one working in those project files every day. I know what I'm seeing. The pattern is right there in the timestamps. The record has been arranged to make my quality control look bad. 

So... no. I wouldn't. I know what's actually happening, regardless of what they claim to show me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly states they would not believe undeniable proof from IT and maintains their belief that the records are being altered to frame them, demonstrating a fixed belief despite contradictory evidence.

turns.doctor_question: Are there any other situations in your life, outside of your work files, that you feel are being manipulated or arranged in a way that others don't seem to recognize?
turns.patient_response:
No. No, nothing else. 

Everything else is... normal. I still translate every day. I manage the workflow for my team. I pay my bills, I see my family... we have our routines. Everything is fine. 

It's just... it's just the files. And those specific people. That's the only thing that's... wrong. Outside of that, everything is exactly as it should be.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient reaffirms their fixed belief that the files and specific people are manipulated or 'wrong'.

No. Not really. 

I mean, I'm tired sometimes, but... I work long hours. That's just part of the job. My sleep is fine. My mood is... fine. 

I'm just trying to do my job. That's all.
